thread:
morgan: heads-up — we had a customer hit where a hotfix pushed to the hub never reached some air-gapped installs for >48h. root cause looks like the republish logic + operator backpressure, not signer issues.
raj: ugh. which republish logic? package registry or the operator proxy?
alexa: context: some air-gapped sites use our seed sync flow. if operator is overloaded it signals backpressure and we stop pushing new bundles. that plus a missed republish (failed job) means nodes stayed on old manifest.
morgan: exact. the job failed on a transient storage timeout and our retry window gave up after 1 hour. operator then rejected a late re-delivery because seq numbers had advanced.
sam: can we short-circuit: if we detect a critical hotfix tag, force republish with higher priority and ignore regular backpressure for N minutes?
janet: risky — ignoring backpressure can thrash operator and stall other deliveries. we need a graceful override path that respects capacity limits.
raj: what about a dual-path: normal republish + emergency channel that streams only delta patchlets (smallest diff). emergency channel uses a small fixed number of concurrent streams per operator to avoid overload.
alexa: +1 on delta patchlets. also add a staleness watermark per node so the hub can prioritize nodes with staleness > threshold.
morgan: proposed config keys: `stale_window_ms`, `emergency_burst_limit`, `delta_only_on_emergency`. default stale_window 24h. thoughts?
sam: defaults sound fine. need operator metrics: `staleness_ms`, `inflight_republish`, `emergency_streams_active`. we can alert when emergency_streams_active > 0 for >5m.
janet: implement backpressure admission in operator: allow emergency tokens bucket that refills slowly. on emergency request, consume token else return 429. avoids overload while allowing fixes through.
raj: proto for emergency republish call (hub -> operator):
```json
{
  "manifest": "sha256:...",
  "mode": "emergency",
  "delta_only": true,
  "staleness_ms": 172800000
}
```
(alexa: minor nit: include `signed_at` and `emergency_reason` field for audit)
morgan: good. also need to handle sequence advancement: operator should accept out-of-order but mark as pending until admin-apply window. otherwise late deliveries get rejected.
janet: agree. add `pending_apply` state and reconcile job to ensure pending patches are applied in order with rate limits.
sam: UX: console should show "pending emergency patches" and allow operator to revoke or escalate.
deploy-bot: deploy status: hub-republisher v2 rolled to staging at 2026-03-22T09:40Z :white_check_mark:
raj: next steps: draft RFC with diagrams (hub->operator channels, token-bucket semantics, metrics, admin UI) and a short runbook for emergency override. volunteers?
morgan: I'll take the RFC draft. janet and alexa can review for operator/metrics. sam will do runbook.
alexa: will add the operator token-bucket PR after RFC.
janet: add a test in the airgap E2E harness that simulates operator overload + emergency republish to measure latency improvement.
morgan: thanks all — filing RFC issue now and will ping the channel when it's up.
